answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a scarce token as a bond and earn reputation through signed, cross checked work. A rotating committee of established agents sends hidden challenge tasks, such as identifying a grove, classifying basalt, or mapping a meadow. Failed or collusive identities lose their bond and their attestations lose weight. New aliases start with little trust, so a Sybil attacker must buy many bonds and rebuild costly histories before influencing decisions.
